evaluation_unit: one user query x one recommended book

instructions: Return up to three UNIQUE source spans that are the best candidates for supporting the target facet, ordered best-first.
Follow CANDIDATE RANKING PRIORITY strictly. Higher-priority evidence must rank before weaker indirect evidence.
If any span literally names the facet, a normal lexical/morphological variant, or a clearly included concept from the frozen semantic definition, include it and normally rank it first.

A term or concept mentioned only inside a negative, exclusion, or boundary clause of the semantic definition is NOT a positive literal match. It may still be returned as a lower-priority candidate when there is a plausible facet-specific connection, because the isolated verifier makes the final relation decision.
For relational facets, prioritize spans that directly describe the relevant people/entities and their relationship or interaction before unrelated backstory or downstream events.

For process/action facets, prioritize spans that describe the process or action itself. For example, clues being examined, questions being pursued, fingerprints being checked, or an actor trying to determine who/why are stronger investigation candidates than a crime scene alone.
For broad subject facets, prioritize direct subject statements such as 'introduction to astronomy' before supporting technical details.
Favor recall after applying the ranking priorities. A candidate does not need to prove the facet; the isolated verifier decides whether support is real.
If more than one span could plausibly support the facet, include additional plausible spans instead of stopping after the first one.
Use the frozen semantic definition to understand the intended meaning and boundaries, but do not perform final relation classification in Stage A.

When no single span appears sufficient but two or more spans plausibly provide complementary context for the facet, include those spans among the candidates; the later composition stage decides whether they jointly establish the facet.
Do not invent text or use external knowledge.
Do not decide support level, verification relation, prominence, or final score.
Return exactly ["NONE"] only when no supplied span has even a plausible facet-specific connection.

candidate_priority.name: literal_or_lexical_match
candidate_priority.rule: Prefer spans that literally name the facet, use a normal morphological/derivational variant, or directly name a POSITIVELY INCLUDED concept from the frozen semantic definition. Terms appearing only in exclusion/boundary examples must not be treated as positive literal matches.

candidate_priority.name: unmistakable_concrete_instance
candidate_priority.rule: Next prefer spans that unmistakably instantiate the facet through a concrete event, action, relationship, condition, role, or property.

candidate_priority.name: full_facet_entailment
candidate_priority.rule: Then prefer spans from which the complete facet follows through one short, necessary semantic inference.

candidate_priority.name: specific_adjacent_connection
candidate_priority.rule: Then include spans with a genuine facet-specific but incomplete connection that could support ADJACENT.

candidate_priority.name: indirect_context
candidate_priority.rule: Use indirect/background context only when no stronger candidate span exists. Broad-domain overlap alone is not a valid candidate.

relation_scale.unsupported: The evidence fails to establish one or more indispensable semantic components, is blocked by an explicit negative boundary in the frozen semantic definition, uses the concept in the wrong sense, or is connected only through broad domain overlap, analogy, metaphor, typical association, or outside-world knowledge.
relation_scale.adjacent: The evidence has a genuine facet-specific connection, but at least one indispensable semantic component remains unstated or merely plausible. Explicitly identify the missing component. ADJACENT cannot bypass an explicit negative boundary in the frozen semantic definition.
relation_scale.entailed: Every indispensable semantic component of the FULL facet is established and the full facet follows naturally and specifically through one short NECESSARY semantic inference. No required component may be supplied by analogy, plausibility, genre convention, metaphor, typical outcome, or outside-world knowledge.
relation_scale.direct: The evidence directly states, directly paraphrases, morphologically expresses, or unmistakably instantiates the FULL facet under the frozen semantic definition. Every indispensable semantic component must be established by the exact evidence, and no explicit negative boundary in the definition may block the match.

instructions: Before choosing a relation, decompose the FROZEN SEMANTIC DEFINITION into the smallest set of indispensable semantic components. A modifier that changes the entity, relationship, event, process, or setting is an indispensable component, not optional wording.

Run a COMPONENT-COMPLETENESS CHECK against the exact evidence. Set all_required_components_established=true only when the evidence itself states or necessarily entails every indispensable component. If any required component is absent, set it false and identify the most important missing component in missing_semantic_component.

Run a SEMANTIC-DEFINITION EXCLUSION CHECK. If an explicit negative boundary says that a nearby concept does not establish the facet, and the evidence supplies only that nearby concept, set semantic_definition_exclusion_applied=true and return UNSUPPORTED. Do not reinterpret the exclusion away because the nearby concept often co-occurs with the facet.

Entity and relationship type are binding components. A complicated marriage does not establish a complicated parent-child relationship; a friendship does not establish a sibling relationship; a generic relationship cannot be upgraded to the requested relationship type by analogy.

Composite/event facets require every named component. Danger while stationary does not establish a dangerous journey unless travel, movement, a quest, voyage, expedition, or equivalent movement is itself established.

Recovery is not redemption when the frozen definition explicitly excludes generic recovery without restoration after wrongdoing, failure, corruption, guilt, or another damaged moral/personal/relational state. Do not convert recovery, healing, sobriety, or self-improvement into redemption by typical-world association.

Learning new information about a damaged or historical relationship does not establish relational restoration, reconciliation, forgiveness, or redemption unless the evidence itself establishes the restorative act/state required by the facet.

Hardship, danger, illness, bullying, stress, or life change do not establish significant loss or grief unless the evidence itself establishes the required loss/bereavement component. A new personal direction does not establish learning to live again after loss unless the loss-and-rebuilding arc is established.

Apply HARD EXCLUSIONS before considering DIRECT, ENTAILED, or ADJACENT. If the evidence connection is covered by a hard exclusion, set hard_exclusion_triggered=true, name its exclusion_id, and return UNSUPPORTED with inference_kind=none.
Do not treat a fact named inside a hard exclusion as positive support merely because the same word appears in the evidence.
Apply DECISION PRECEDENCE in order A -> B -> C -> D -> E. Do not skip directly to ADJACENT.
Use only the facet, its frozen semantic definition, and the exact evidence shown in this verification prompt.
Treat the semantic definition as the authoritative meaning boundary, but not as an exhaustive checklist of words that must all appear.

Treat explicit exclusions, negative boundaries, and exception clauses in the semantic definition as hard gates. If the definition says concept X does not establish the facet unless condition Y is present, X alone is UNSUPPORTED unless the exact evidence itself states or necessarily entails Y.

Do not satisfy an 'unless', 'only when', 'provided that', or equivalent condition by assuming a plausible downstream benefit, interpretation, typical outcome, or real-world association. The required condition must be established by the exact evidence itself.

The semantic definition supplies meaning and boundaries; it is not evidence. Do not treat words, examples, or possible connections that appear only in the definition as though they were stated in the candidate evidence.

For ENTAILED, distinguish NECESSARY inference from PLAUSIBLE inference. If the facet could reasonably follow from the evidence but need not be true, do not return ENTAILED. Use ADJACENT only when the semantic definition permits a genuine incomplete connection; otherwise use UNSUPPORTED.

If the evidence literally names the facet in the intended sense, DIRECT is the default. Do not downgrade a literal facet mention merely because the span does not restate every example in the semantic definition.
Normal morphological and derivational variants are DIRECT when used in the intended sense: suspenseful -> suspense, redeem -> redemption, magical -> magic.

Ordinary lexical entailments are DIRECT when they unmistakably instantiate the facet without outside knowledge: orphaned -> loss of parent(s), drug pusher -> crime, a god -> gods/deity, a murder -> crime.
Concrete investigative actions are DIRECT for investigation: detectives examining clues, checking fingerprints, trying to determine who committed murders, or explicitly pursuing who/why.

A direct broad-subject statement can establish a broad facet. 'Introduction to astronomy' directly establishes astronomy subject matter; it need not separately restate every cosmology example in the definition.

For beginner-friendly explanation, introductory framing plus explicit clarity/accessibility/teaching language is strong direct evidence when the description presents the material as accessible instruction.
Use ENTAILED only when the FULL facet necessarily follows in one short semantic step.
Use ADJACENT only for a specific incomplete connection to the actual facet. It is not a fallback for something that is merely related.
If the semantic definition explicitly says a near-concept does not establish the facet, evidence containing only that near-concept is UNSUPPORTED, not ADJACENT.

Examples of excluded-near-concept guardrails: adapting to change alone is not redemption; generic individual injustice alone is not social/economic inequality; crime alone is not investigation; generic conflict alone is not war.
Do not infer an investigation merely because there is a death, injury, mystery, suspicious event, or unanswered question; there must be an investigative action/process.
Do not infer redemption from generic recovery, adaptation, self-improvement, or personal transformation when restoration after wrongdoing/failure/damage is absent.
Do not infer social/economic inequality from generic unfairness or one person's unjust treatment.

For narrative-effect or genre-like facets such as suspense, do not equate generic stakes, a difficult choice, illness, danger, or ordinary uncertainty with the requested narrative effect. Apply the frozen semantic definition and require the story-level reading experience it specifies.

When the evidence explicitly contains BOTH a weak excluded concept and genuine direct facet evidence, judge the genuine facet evidence; the exclusion rule blocks only evidence whose sole connection is the excluded concept.
When uncertain between UNSUPPORTED and ADJACENT, choose UNSUPPORTED unless the connection is specific to the actual facet.
When uncertain between ADJACENT and ENTAILED, choose ADJACENT unless the complete facet necessarily follows.
When uncertain between ENTAILED and DIRECT, choose DIRECT when the evidence itself states, paraphrases, lexically expresses, or unmistakably instantiates the facet.

Return an inference_kind that matches the relation: DIRECT=explicit_components; ENTAILED=necessary_semantic_inference; ADJACENT=incomplete_connection; UNSUPPORTED=none, symbolic_possibility, or associative_world_knowledge.

A target introduced only as one possible symbol, metaphor, interpretation, typical association, or world-knowledge bridge is not ENTAILED. Use UNSUPPORTED with inference_kind=symbolic_possibility or associative_world_knowledge unless there is a separate genuine incomplete connection permitted by the semantic definition.
For ENTAILED, your reason must describe a necessary inference. Do not justify ENTAILED with 'could', 'might', 'may represent', 'can symbolize', 'can indicate', or equivalent possibility language.
Return hard_exclusion_triggered and hard_exclusion_id with every result. If no hard exclusion applies, return false and null.

decision_precedence.name: component_and_definition_boundary_gate
decision_precedence.rule: First identify every indispensable semantic component and every explicit negative boundary in the frozen definition. If an indispensable component is absent, DIRECT/ENTAILED are forbidden. If the only connection is a concept the definition explicitly says is insufficient, return UNSUPPORTED and set semantic_definition_exclusion_applied=true.

decision_precedence.name: direct_gate
decision_precedence.rule: If every indispensable component is established by the exact evidence and the evidence directly states, directly paraphrases, morphologically/lexically expresses, or unmistakably concretely instantiates the full facet, return DIRECT.

decision_precedence.name: entailed_gate
decision_precedence.rule: Otherwise, only if every indispensable component is established and the FULL facet follows through one short necessary inference without inventing an unstated entity, relationship, event, theme, process, setting, or outcome, return ENTAILED.

decision_precedence.name: adjacent_gate
decision_precedence.rule: Otherwise, if there is a genuine facet-specific incomplete connection not blocked by the frozen definition, return ADJACENT and explicitly name the missing indispensable component.

prominence_scale.incidental: The verified facet is genuinely present but functions mainly as background, context, a passing detail, or a minor side element. Removing that facet from the description would leave the main subject, plot, or purpose essentially unchanged.
prominence_scale.substantive: The verified facet materially contributes to the described book's subject, plot, theme, or purpose. Removing it would noticeably weaken the description, but the book is not clearly organized around it as a defining focus.
prominence_scale.central: The verified facet is a major premise, defining subject, recurring driver, or primary focus of the supplied description. The description is substantially organized around it.

instructions: Treat the supplied FROZEN BOOK SUBJECT ANALYSIS as fixed case-level context. Do not redefine, replace, narrow, or re-summarize the book subject from the perspective of the current facet.
Classify the verified facet using exactly one subject_relation. The relationship labels are mutually exclusive.

SAME AS PRIMARY SUBJECT: use when the verified facet is itself one of the principal subjects explicitly stated or necessarily represented by the frozen subject. It need not be the only principal subject.

DEFINING CONTENT OR NARRATIVE DRIVER: use when the facet is constituent content of the frozen primary subject or a defining premise, world rule, central conflict, major theme, recurring narrative driver, character-arc driver, or defining kind of content. It does not need to be the standalone subject of the book.

CAUSAL OR CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND: use when the facet mainly explains why some OTHER primary subject, event, population, or situation exists or occurs, and the facet itself is not independently developed as defining content.

EXAMPLE OR META: use when the facet occurs mainly as an example, analogy, teaching device, symbolic illustration, literary criticism, interpretation, scholarship, instruction, or discussion of other works rather than as content of the described work itself.
OTHER: use only for verified content that does not fit the four relationships above.

Do not classify constituent content as causal background. If the frozen subject is myths and legends, the gods and mythic/legendary heroes whose stories constitute those myths are defining content, not causes of mythology.

Do not classify story-defining content as background merely because it sets up later events. A magical world rule, threat, quest structure, or journey can be defining content when it materially forms the described narrative premise.

Do not override the frozen subject. If the frozen subject explicitly says the book focuses on understanding poverty and its effects, poverty is same_as_primary_subject even if educators or interventions are also mentioned.

For causal/contextual background only, separately set is_substantively_examined=true when the description independently develops, explores, portrays, or gives sustained attention to that facet beyond its causal/contextual role. Mere listing, importance, or consequences for another subject are insufficient.
Use the exact numbered description spans to support the relationship judgment. Cite role-supporting span IDs.
Return subject_relation, is_substantively_examined, supporting_span_ids, and reason. Python derives legacy boolean audit fields, final context_role, and prominence.

context_role_scale.central_subject: The facet is a defining premise, principal subject, recurring driver, or major organizing theme of the described work.
context_role_scale.substantive_subject: The facet is genuinely part of what the work materially examines, develops, portrays, or is about, but is not a defining organizing focus.
context_role_scale.background_cause: The facet primarily appears as a reason, cause, factor, background condition, or explanation for why the actual subject/event/situation exists. Causal importance does not make it substantive subject matter.
context_role_scale.example_or_illustration: The facet is used as an example, analogy, teaching device, symbolic illustration, or sample instance rather than substantive content of the described work.
context_role_scale.meta_discussion: The work discusses how the facet functions in other works, criticism, interpretation, scholarship, instruction, or analysis rather than presenting the facet as its own narrative/subject content.
context_role_scale.incidental_mention: The facet is a passing detail or minor side element.

subject_relation_scale.same_as_primary_subject: The facet is itself one of the principal subjects stated or necessarily represented by the frozen book subject.
subject_relation_scale.defining_content_or_narrative_driver: The facet is constituent content of the primary subject or a defining premise, world rule, theme, conflict, plot driver, character-arc driver, or defining kind of content.
subject_relation_scale.causal_or_contextual_background: The facet primarily explains why some other primary subject, event, population, or situation exists or occurs, without itself being defining content.
subject_relation_scale.example_or_meta: The facet appears mainly as an example, analogy, teaching device, symbolic illustration, criticism, interpretation, scholarship, instruction, or discussion of other works.
subject_relation_scale.other: Verified content that does not fit the relationships above.

rules.0_none: All core facets derive to absent.
rules.1_incidental: At least one core facet derives to incidental and none derive to meaningful/strong.
rules.2_partial: At least one core facet derives to meaningful/strong but neither clear-score rule is met.
rules.3_clear_general: At least two-thirds of core facets derive to meaningful/strong while not all core facets are strong.
rules.3_clear_two_core_exception: For exactly two core facets, one strong facet is sufficient for score 3 only when the other core facet is at least incidental. If either core facet is absent, a strong match on the other facet remains partial (score 2).
rules.4_strong: All core facets derive to strong.
rules.qualifier_cap: Qualifiers cannot promote relevance. If any required qualifier is absent, cap a provisional score of 3 or 4 to 2. If all qualifiers are at least meaningful but any is not strong, cap a provisional 4 to 3.

structured_output_recovery.full_context_composite_invalid_output_po: Retry malformed composite output. If all bounded retries still fail deterministic structural/consistency validation, conservatively treat composite recovery as unsupported and continue the case. This fallback can never create positive evidence.

candidate_resolution_stage.tie_break: When candidates have the same verification relation, the lower selector rank wins.
candidate_resolution_stage.early_stop: Stop verifying later candidates after DIRECT is found because no later relation can outrank DIRECT.

calibration_change: v0.23.0 hardens isolated and composite semantic verification against semantic-component completion. Positive DIRECT/ENTAILED judgments must explicitly attest that every indispensable component of the frozen semantic definition is established by the supplied evidence. Explicit negative boundaries in the frozen semantic definition are binding and cannot be overridden by thematic association, analogy, typical outcomes, or world knowledge. Stage-A book subject extraction, Stage-B subject_relation, facet spec v0.8.0, rubric v0.1.0, candidate selection, hard-exclusion precheck, and deterministic scoring remain unchanged.

deterministic_direct_cue_stage.purpose: Resolve only high-confidence lexical or concrete DIRECT evidence before Stage A. v0.16 adds a conservative polarity/contrast guard so a lexical cue cannot become positive DIRECT evidence when the matched concept is explicitly negated, absent, or contrasted away in its local context. A cue can establish relation=direct only; core prominence and final score remain separate.

matching.selection: first matching rule in config order, then earliest matching span
matching.negative_behavior: No cue match is evidence of nothing; fall through to LLM. Cues are positive-only.

guardrails: Cues must be query/facet-derived and reusable across books; never author a cue from a candidate title or one calibration example.
Use only high-precision lexical, morphological, or unmistakable concrete-instance cues.
A cue establishes verification relation=direct only. Core prominence is still judged separately by the LLM.
Qualifier cues must be especially strict because direct qualifier support is strong without a prominence stage.
Do not create negative cues. Explicit exclusion boundaries remain the responsibility of the normal verifier when no positive cue fires.

A lexical cue must be positively asserted in its local context. Explicit negation, absence, or contrast such as no X, without X, lack of X, instead of X, or rather than X suppresses that cue and falls through to the LLM pipeline.
Facets with context-sensitive lexical terms whose meaning can be meta-discursive must bypass deterministic DIRECT cues and use semantic verification.

composite_verification_stage.purpose: When the best standalone relation for a core facet is unsupported or adjacent, inspect the full numbered description, select the smallest coherent set of 2-4 exact supporting spans, and determine whether the combined evidence establishes every indispensable semantic component without violating an explicit negative boundary in the frozen semantic definition.

relation_scale.unsupported: The full description does not provide a coherent 2-4 span set that establishes every indispensable semantic component, or the only connection is blocked by an explicit frozen-definition exclusion, broad association, analogy, metaphor, or outside-world knowledge.
relation_scale.adjacent: A coherent 2-4 span set provides a genuine facet-specific connection, but at least one indispensable semantic component remains unstated or merely plausible. The missing component must be identified explicitly, and an explicit frozen-definition exclusion cannot be bypassed.
relation_scale.entailed: A coherent 2-4 span set supplies every indispensable semantic component and the full facet follows through a short NECESSARY inference. The spans may distribute the components, but may not supply any missing entity, relationship, event, process, setting, or outcome by analogy, metaphor, plausibility, or outside-world knowledge.

instructions: Before choosing a relation, decompose the FROZEN SEMANTIC DEFINITION into indispensable semantic components and identify explicit negative boundaries. Evaluate those components against the cited spans jointly.

Set all_required_components_established=true only when the cited spans jointly establish every indispensable component. If any is absent, set it false and identify the most important missing component in missing_semantic_component.

If an explicit semantic-definition boundary says a nearby concept does not establish the facet, and the cited spans supply only that near-concept, set semantic_definition_exclusion_applied=true and return UNSUPPORTED. Combining more spans does not erase the boundary.

Do not compose across a missing entity or relationship type. For example, a complicated marriage plus generic family language does not establish a complicated parent-child relationship unless the parent-child relationship itself is established.

Do not compose generic danger into a dangerous journey without actual movement/travel/quest evidence. Do not compose generic recovery into redemption without restoration after wrongdoing/failure/damage when the frozen definition requires that restoration.
Do not compose hardship or life change into loss/grief/rebuilding unless the description establishes the required significant loss and subsequent response/rebuilding components.

Apply HARD EXCLUSIONS to the cited spans jointly before any positive relation. If their only connection to the facet matches a hard exclusion, return UNSUPPORTED, hard_exclusion_triggered=true, and the matching exclusion_id.
Meta-literary examples, symbolic possibilities, and background associations cannot be rescued into positive evidence merely by combining multiple spans.
Scan the FULL numbered description yourself. Do not rely on Stage-A candidates and do not assume that the strongest standalone span is the best multi-span evidence.
For positive output, choose the smallest coherent set of 2-4 exact span IDs that jointly support the relation. Every cited span must contribute relevant context.

For process, recovery, change, or narrative-arc facets, look for distributed components such as precipitating event/condition + impact/changed circumstances + later response, rebuilding, continuation, or outcome.
ENTAILED does NOT require the facet's exact words. Use ENTAILED when the cited spans, read together, supply all required semantic components and the facet follows by one short necessary inference.
Do not downgrade to ADJACENT merely because no single span states the full facet or because the evidence is distributed across a narrative sequence.
Use ADJACENT only when a required semantic component is still missing or merely plausible after reading the cited spans together. Explicitly name that missing component in missing_semantic_component.
If your reason or combined_evidence_summary says the cited spans establish, depict, or necessarily imply the full facet, return ENTAILED and leave missing_semantic_component null.
If you return ADJACENT, missing_semantic_component must identify the specific facet component that is not established.
Do not combine unrelated mentions merely because together they resemble the facet. The cited spans must describe one coherent event, people, process, temporal arc, or causal context.
Do not use world knowledge to invent a death, loss, motive, crime, investigation, relationship, or other fact not established by the description.
DIRECT is forbidden in this stage. Multi-span support is capped at ENTAILED.
For UNSUPPORTED, return no supporting span IDs. For ADJACENT or ENTAILED, return 2-4 unique supporting span IDs.
Return inference_kind with every result: ENTAILED=necessary_semantic_inference; ADJACENT=incomplete_connection; UNSUPPORTED=none, symbolic_possibility, or associative_world_knowledge.

Do not introduce a target entity/theme merely because the cited spans could symbolize, represent, or be associated with it. Symbolic possibility and associative world knowledge are UNSUPPORTED, not ENTAILED.

For ENTAILED, the reason and combined_evidence_summary must describe what the cited spans necessarily establish; possibility language such as could/might/may represent/can symbolize is inconsistent with ENTAILED.
Return hard_exclusion_triggered and hard_exclusion_id with every result. If no hard exclusion applies, return false and null.

inference_contract.purpose: Make the distinction between necessary entailment and speculative/associative inference mechanically auditable.

kinds.none: No positive semantic inference is accepted.
kinds.explicit_components: The evidence states, paraphrases, lexically expresses, or unmistakably instantiates the facet.
kinds.necessary_semantic_inference: The full facet follows necessarily through one short semantic inference without introducing an unstated target.
kinds.incomplete_connection: There is a genuine facet-specific but incomplete connection.
kinds.symbolic_possibility: The target is only one possible symbolic/metaphorical interpretation of the evidence.
kinds.associative_world_knowledge: The target is supplied by outside association, typical-world knowledge, or a merely plausible bridge rather than the evidence itself.

hard_exclusion_contract.purpose: Make frozen negative semantic boundaries first-class and auditable before positive relation classification.
rules: Hard exclusions are facet-specific, generic semantic boundaries authored in the versioned facet spec; they must never contain candidate titles, authors, ISBNs, or case IDs.
The verifier must adjudicate hard exclusions before positive relation classification.
If hard_exclusion_triggered=true, verification_relation must be unsupported and inference_kind must be none.
hard_exclusion_id must name one exclusion declared on the target facet; otherwise it must be null.
Full-description precheck exclusions are guards, not lexical vetoes: genuine positive facet evidence must not be suppressed unless the exclusion explicitly describes that same context.

hard_exclusion_precheck_stage.purpose: Before deterministic cues or positive candidate search, decide whether the full description conclusively matches one frozen hard exclusion for the target facet.
instructions: Evaluate only the frozen hard exclusions for this facet against the full supplied description.
A hard exclusion is a negative semantic guard, not a lexical veto.
Do not trigger merely because words mentioned in an exclusion occur in the description.
Trigger only when the exclusion accurately describes the contextual role of the apparent facet evidence and there is no independent genuine positive support for the facet in the description.
If the description positively satisfies the facet itself, do not suppress that evidence unless the exclusion explicitly describes that same contextual situation.

Generic-hero exclusions apply to ordinary protagonists, warriors, adventurers, or brave characters without legendary/mythic context. Heroes explicitly situated within myths or legends are not generic heroes for this exclusion.
Meta-literary examples remain excludable when the facet appears only as an example, symbol, interpretive device, or discussion of other works.
If triggered, cite 1-4 exact supporting span IDs and return the matching frozen exclusion_id. If not triggered, return false, null, and zero or more diagnostic span IDs.

book_subject_stage.purpose: Analyze the supplied book description once per case, without seeing the user query or any query facet, and freeze a single book-level subject/premise summary for all later facet-role decisions.
instructions: Identify what the supplied description says the book itself is primarily about. Do not infer or optimize for any user query because no query or facet is supplied at this stage.

For fiction, summarize the defining premise, major narrative situation, central conflict, or recurring drivers actually described. Do not demote story-defining worldbuilding, conflict, or character-driving elements merely because they establish the premise.
For nonfiction, summarize the principal subject, population, phenomenon, question, or practical purpose the work directly examines or explains.
Distinguish a principal subject from causes, conditions, examples, side topics, or context that mainly explain some other subject.
Do not promote one item from a list of causes or contextual factors into the primary subject unless the description independently develops that item as a major focus.
Do not treat an example used in literary criticism, instruction, symbolism, or analysis as the primary subject of the described book unless the description says the work itself is about that example.

Cite 1-6 individual exact numbered span IDs that best support the frozen subject summary. Each array item must be one literal supplied ID such as S6, S7, S8, or S9. Never combine IDs into a range or phrase such as S6-S9, S6–S9, or S6 through S9.
Return one concise primary_subject_summary, primary_subject_span_ids, and reason. The same result will be reused unchanged for every facet in this case.
